title: Nura: Rise of the Yokai Clan
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Rikuo Nura, a schoolboy who is one-quarter yokai, is human by day and a yokai lord by night. Chosen by his grandfather Nurarihyon as heir to a powerful yokai clan run like a crime syndicate, he must win the loyalty of rival factions and fight threats such as the nine-tailed fox Hagoromo Gitsune in Kyoto, eventually uniting yokai clans across Japan (Wikipedia; Viz blurb via AniList; ANN).
life_message: A good leader earns loyalty by protecting both humans and yokai and by showing mercy to defeated rivals.

content.note: Sword and supernatural battles throughout, deaths of clan members (Wikipedia; ANN 'action-packed'; AniList Swordplay; MU War, Death of Loved One).
Yokai horror elements; a yokai who wants to eat humans (Viz blurb; AniList Horror genre; MU Monsters).
Light schoolboy romance; MangaDex rates it safe.
Sake drinking at clan gatherings is a common motif (to verify).
Day and night selves (AniList Dissociative Identities 70; MU Split Personality), framed as fantasy.

dominant: Heirship and loyalty; human-yokai coexistence; Japanese folklore

frames.aligns: Rikuo spares Tamazuki and protects humans; leadership as service.
frames.concerns: Yokai and onmyoji spirit powers as heroes; mafia-style clan; occult imagery.

frames.aligns: Mercy and protection of the weak.
frames.concerns: Demonic and spirit beings presented as allies.
Hero is part-demon leading spirits; exorcism and shikigami (MU).
Spirit and demon heroes; onmyodo magic.
Demons and spirits as heroes is an open door concern.

frames.aligns: Duty of an heir to his house.
Honor of grandfather and clan duty.
Folklore fantasy framing good and evil clearly.
Bridging human and yokai worlds; Rikuo defends yokai to classmates.

frames.concerns: Spirits and magic shown as good; onmyodo sorcery.

frames.aligns: Dharma of an heir; spirits part of the world.

frames.concerns: Supernatural as fiction only, little concern.
Ghosts and spirits as real and friendly.

frames.aligns: Pluralism of human and yokai worlds.
Folk spirits honored; nature beings as kin.
Yokai, kami-like spirits and ancestors treated with familiarity and respect.
Spiritual beings and a hidden self.
Embracing one's darker nature with pride.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Clan challenges must be answered in battle to prove the heir (Wikipedia; ANN).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Clan rules and a council of sub-leaders (ANN).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Bloodline heirship and sworn clan family (Wikipedia; MU Strong Family).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Third Heir, board members and sworn subordinates (Wikipedia).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Folklore, onmyoji houses and ancestral blades (Wikipedia; MU Folklore).

folkways.japan: The clan is modeled on yakuza family structure and draws on Japanese yokai folklore, Kyoto and the onmyoji tradition of Abe no Seimei.

delivery.evidence: ANN: themes of heirship and loyalty come through battles and clan debates; a rebel's scheme is called 'well-intentioned'.

personified.ideology: testing a weak heir by force for the clan's good

delivery.note: Some rivals are given sympathetic backstories and spared, while others who see humans as food are plain monsters.

winners_losers: Rikuo wins the loyalty of yokai clans; usurpers and the human-hating sect are defeated. Sympathy goes to a leader who bridges both worlds.
to_verify: Gagoze's portrayal beyond the Viz blurb
Level of gore in later arcs (AniList lists Horror genre)
